text:
sania: Quick brain-dump: proposing an 'admit-sieve' service that performs lightweight validation & emits compact patches (token remaps, header meta, runtime hints) instead of always producing a full normalized binary. Goal: keep ingest fast, limit duplicate storage, and still give runtime a clear contract. Thoughts?

liam: Sounds useful. How do we guarantee that the first request doesn't suffer if runtime needs to apply a patch-on-load?

zara: Plan is header-first decisioning: runtime reads the header/manifest and immediately knows whether it can serve as-is, needs to apply a patch-sync, or must route to a fallback adapter. For latency-sensitive orgs we can pre-materialize.

adele: How about semantic safety? Token remaps can subtly shift outputs. We should require a reversible remapping file and a tiny replay harness that runs a handful of representative prompts on original vs patched to compute overlap. If divergence > threshold -> manual triage.

mike: Agree. To minimize GPU churn, run a cheap CPU-based top-k overlap probe first (using a tiny quantized reference). Only escalate to a short GPU micro-run if CPU probe flags or model size > threshold.

ops-bot: Heads-up: ingest concurrency cap is 12. If many rehydrate events happen, we may see queue pressure. Recommend a prioritized rehydrate queue and backoff.

liam: For tokenizer equality, propose a deterministic 'token-sig' computed from vocab + special token ordering + normalization rules. Emit that sig and the remap patch. If token-sig mismatch but replay overlap high, AUTO-APPROVE per rule engine.

sania: Rule engine sounds necessary. Make rules ordered and environment-scoped: example predicate order: FAIL overrides WARN, WARN logs, AUTO-APPROVE applies patch and records audit. Keep rule syntax simple YAML so SRE/Support can tweak thresholds.

zara: Metrics for the replay harness: top1/top5 overlap, per-token logprob delta for gold tokens, and latency p50/p95. Store the small replay trace and link to the triage UI.

adele: Manifest design: compact index with manifest_v, model_id, file checksums, token_sig, patch_refs, quick-sanity fields (cpu_probe: true/false, top5: 0.xx). That way registry queries can be cheap.

liam: Sketch manifest example (inline):
```
manifest_v: 1
model_id: org/foo/exp
files: [weights.pt, tokenizer.json]
checksums: [w:abcd, t:ef01]
token_sig: tok-2026-1
patches: [tok-remap-v1]
sanity: {cpu_probe:true, top5:0.95}
```

mike: Operational concerns: If many patches are stored, registry grows. Lazy materialization reduces that but increases complexity at runtime. Estimate initial storage delta if materialize-all: +6-10%. Recommend lazy-by-default, materialize-on-pinned or enterprise flag.

sania: Agreed. Also need an audit trail for compliance: who approved an AUTO-APPROVE, timestamps, and the reversible patch file. Triage UI should expose these and let an operator revert a patch.

ops-bot: Note: adding an indexable 'patches' field requires registry migration. Suggest write-new, read-old+new strategy to avoid flapping failures.

zara: Canary plan: pick a small set of internal orgs, admit via sieve with patches recorded but not yet applied to production runtime. Shadow-serve traffic for 48-72h comparing raw vs patched outputs. Thresholds: top1 overlap >= 0.92 and logprob-delta mean < 0.2 for green. Otherwise rollback.

adele: For remap generation: make remap deterministic and reversible. Also produce a confidence score (how many token collisions remapped heuristically). If collisions > X => semantic-risk flag.

liam: We should also version the header schema and require runtime to tolerate unknown keys (ignore+warn) until we roll adapters. Keep header additions additive.

mike: Monitoring: record which path served a request (raw, patched-on-load, materialized). Expose counts and errors per org/model so we can detect regressions quickly.

sania: OK next steps: Adele protos a tokenizer signature + reversible remapper. Liam builds a minimal rule-engine YAML and manifest sketch. Zara drafts the canary runbook and thresholds. I'll prototype a tiny ingest-sieve service to emit patches. Reconvene in 48h.

ops-bot: Reminder: plan capacity bump +15% for the initial canary to cover GPU micro-runs and rehydrations.

registry-bot: Migration note: adding 'patches' and 'sanity' fields => registry schema migration window. Use feature flag gating.

sania: Thanks all. I'll drop the prototype branch + a short diagram into #eng-ml-docs. Ping me if you want early access to the harness.
